title: U.S. House · Indiana's 9th District
area: Southeastern Indiana, including Columbus, Seymour, Madison, and the Ohio River counties.

context.text: Incumbent Erin Houchin ran unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Brad Meyer won the Democratic primary with 37.9% in a four-way field. Tonya Hudson advanced from the Libertarian Party's March 22, 2026 convention. Floyd Taylor filed as a declared write-in independent candidate.

summary.text: Erin Houchin is the Republican incumbent for Indiana's 9th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A Salem native, she ran a communications firm, worked for U.S. Senator Dan Coats's regional office, and served eight years in the Indiana Senate before moving to Congress. She is seeking a second full term after advancing unopposed from the May 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Born in Salem, Indiana, in 1976, and describes herself as a native of the 9th District.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Indiana University and a master's degree in political management from George Washington University.

Career experience includes owning a business, founding and serving as president of Contend Communications, and working for the Indiana Department of Child Services, Community Alliance Promoting Education, New Hope Services, and Prevent Child Abuse Indiana. Her official biography also says she operated a communications firm focused on helping law enforcement communicate their work.

In 2011, served as southeast Indiana regional director for U.S. Senator Dan Coats (R). Held local party roles including 9th District chair of the Indiana Republican Party, 9th District chair of the Indiana Federation of Republican Women, and vice chair of the Washington County Republican Party, and was a governor's appointee to the Indiana Commission for Women.
Ran in the 2016 Republican primary for Indiana's 9th Congressional District, which Trey Hollingsworth won.

Won the Indiana State Senate District 47 seat in 2014, defeating Democratic incumbent Richard D. Young Jr. in the general election, and was re-elected in 2018. Served in the state Senate for eight years, including as ranking member on Tax and Fiscal Policy.

Won the open 9th District U.S. House seat in 2022, defeating Democrat Matthew Fyfe, Libertarian Tonya Hudson, and write-in candidate Jacob Bailey in the general election, and took office January 3, 2023, succeeding Hollingsworth. She was re-elected in 2024.

In the 118th Congress (2023-2024), served on the Committees on Education and the Workforce, Financial Services, and Rules. Her official biography lists her current committee assignments as Rules, Budget, and Energy and Commerce.

Ballotpedia lists an endorsement from President Donald Trump. According to her official biography, she is married to Dustin (married 2002), they have three children, and the family lives in Washington County, Indiana.

priorities.text: Campaign website says she supports President Trump's border security efforts, including finishing the wall and deporting criminal immigrants in the country illegally.
priorities.quote: She fully supports President Trump’s efforts to restore border security—by backing law enforcement, finishing the wall, and deporting criminal illegal aliens to protect American communities.

priorities.text: Campaign website says she is a fiscal conservative who supports a Balanced Budget Amendment and cutting government spending.
priorities.quote: Erin is a committed fiscal conservative and has the track record to prove it, and as a champion for Indiana’s Balanced Budget Amendment, she is bringing that same fiscal discipline to Washington.

priorities.text: Campaign website says the government should get out of the way of small businesses, citing cutting red tape, promoting free markets, and controlling spending.
priorities.quote: Erin knows the best way to create jobs and grow the economy is to get the government out of the way and let small business owners do what they do best

positions.summary: Campaign website says she is pro-life and has advocated for prohibiting late-term abortions.
positions.quote: Erin is pro-life and always has been. She has been a steadfast leader in the fight for the unborn, consistently advocating for the prohibition of late-term abortions

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will fight to ensure police officers have the resources, support, and compensation they need, and opposes defunding the police.
positions.quote: Erin will always fight to ensure our officers have the necessary resources to do their jobs effectively and safely, and they have the support and compensation they deserve. Erin will never allow radical left-wing politicians to defund the police.

positions.summary: In a candidate survey for WFYI and Louisville Public Media, lists barring transgender athletes from women's sports among the liberties she says she will defend.
positions.quote: keeping biological men out of women's sports

candidates.name: Brad Meyer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.9% of the vote in a four-way field.

summary.text: Brad Meyer is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 9th Congressional District. A Brownsburg native and Purdue graduate, he worked about 25 years in manufacturing, then as a Navy civilian engineer at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane. According to his campaign, he is running on affordability, Medicare for All, and defending democratic institutions; he has been endorsed by Indivisible Southeast Indiana and the Progressive Voters Network.

background.text: Born in Brownsburg, Indiana, and graduated from Brownsburg High School. Describes himself as a seventh-generation Hoosier.
Earned a bachelor's degree (1989) and a graduate degree (1998) from Purdue University in Indianapolis, according to Ballotpedia; his campaign says he studied electronics engineering at Purdue.

According to his campaign website, spent 25 years in local manufacturing, in work ranging from sensor and electronics assembly to machining, heat treat, and plating, including management roles. In his Ballotpedia survey he says he worked up to Engineering Manager.

According to his campaign website, moved to Bloomington in 2010 to support Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane, and was hired as a Navy civilian engineer in 2016, spending nine years working in electromagnetic warfare.
Says he left his job a year short of early retirement to run for office. Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 37.9% of the vote in a four-way race.
Says he married his high school sweetheart at 18 and that they put themselves through Purdue together.

priorities.text: Says wages have stalled while housing, healthcare, and education costs have squeezed middle-class families, and calls for economic reforms aimed at fairness.
priorities.quote: Wages have stalled while costs keep rising. Housing, healthcare, and education are squeezing families into bankruptcy.

priorities.text: Supports building on Medicare to guarantee universal healthcare coverage.
priorities.quote: Universal healthcare is a proven solution. By building on programs like Medicare, we can guarantee coverage for every resident, end medical bankruptcies, and free people to choose their doctor without fear of financial ruin.

priorities.text: Says he will work to restore institutional checks on power and protect the Department of Education from what he describes as partisan threats.

positions.summary: Supports building on Medicare toward universal healthcare coverage.
positions.quote: By building on programs like Medicare, we can guarantee coverage for every resident, end medical bankruptcies, and free people to choose their doctor without fear of financial ruin.

positions.summary: States on his campaign site that mass deportation would cost billions and shrink the economy, and calls for legal pathways and legalizing the status of immigrants already contributing.
positions.quote: Mass deportation would cost billions more and shrink the economy.

positions.summary: Calls the U.S. commitment to net-zero carbon emissions by 2035 a timely but achievable goal and describes fossil fuel companies as discrediting climate science.
positions.quote: The United States has committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2035. That is a timely but achievable goal

positions.summary: Campaign site policy list includes taxing capital gains for top earners as regular income and eliminating tax loopholes used by the ultra-wealthy.
positions.quote: Tax capital gains for top earners as regular income.

positions.summary: Campaign site policy list includes establishing a $20 per hour national minimum wage.
Campaign site calls for rolling back tariffs, saying they drive up the cost of goods for families.
positions.quote: Roll back tariffs that drive up the daily cost of goods for families.

candidates.name: Tonya Hudson
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party's March 22, 2026 convention.

summary.text: Tonya Hudson is the Libertarian nominee for Indiana's 9th Congressional District, a real estate broker born in Indianapolis who has run in prior elections on reducing taxes and government regulation.

background.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana, and graduated from John Marshall High School.

Works as a real estate broker in southern Indiana; her Ballotpedia profile lists affiliations with the Lions Club and the Indiana Association of Realtors. Earlier, she recalls working as a health aide in the Brown County High School nurse's office around 2001.
Ran as the Libertarian candidate for Indiana's 9th Congressional District in 2022, finishing third with 2.8% of the vote (6,374 votes) in the race won by Erin Houchin.

Ran as the Libertarian candidate for Lieutenant Governor of Indiana in 2024, winning 4.5% (129,781 votes); Micah Beckwith (R) won the office. She was selected at the Libertarian state convention over Tommy Brown III.
Advanced from the Libertarian convention for the 9th District on March 22, 2026.

priorities.text: Supports reducing the tax burden, abolishing the IRS, and rolling back regulations she says hinder small businesses, farmers, and entrepreneurs.
priorities.quote: We, as a People, need to reduce the tax burden and give the people their money back. Abolish the IRS. Roll back the rules, regulations and red tape that hinder small businesses, farmers and entrepreneurs from becoming successful.

priorities.text: Lists voting against unconstitutional wars among her top priorities.

statements.quote: The unauthorized war in Iran by DJT has been a disaster.
statements.context: On her campaign site, on the wars in the Middle East

statements.quote: The good citizens of this land have the right to keep and bear Arms. Period.
If elected, as a member of Congress, I will endorse pro-climate bills to influence positive change around our planet without increasing taxes on the American People.

We need to add more entry-check points to reduce the bottle neck of traffic while at the same time update/streamline the processing system to make it easier for migrant workers to come into the U.S. legally.
statements.context: On her campaign site, under "Secure Borders and Immigration"

statements.quote: We, as a People, need to reduce the tax burden and give the people their money back. Abolish the IRS.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements are from her campaign site, her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and the Louisville Public Media/WFYI candidate survey. She says on her site that military assistance to allies should be authorized by Congress only as an exception; that sentence is unclear on the guide issue and is not recorded.

candidates.name: Floyd Taylor
candidates.ballotNote: Declared write-in candidate for the general election.

summary.text: Floyd Taylor is an independent write-in candidate for Indiana's 9th Congressional District, a local business owner and cancer survivor, according to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working as a computer engineer.

In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, describes himself as a Hoosier, husband, and local business owner, and a network architect with more than 25 years of experience securing critical infrastructure for institutions including Jefferson Public Radio, Fort Knox, Purdue University, and the U.S. Census Bureau.

Says he built the Congress App (thecongressapp.com), which he describes as publishing bills in plain language with fiscal breakdowns and letting verified district constituents weigh in. He says he takes no PAC or party money.
Is running as a write-in independent in the November 3, 2026 general election; Ballotpedia lists no prior candidacies for him.

priorities.text: Says his votes would be bound to what verified district constituents say through the Congress App.
priorities.quote: My vote is bound to what the district says — not what a party whip demands.

priorities.text: Says rural infrastructure and health care access are policy priorities.
priorities.quote: Southern Indiana doesn't need more speeches. It needs broadband that reaches the last mile, healthcare that reaches rural counties, dementia care for the veterans who earned it, property tax relief for seniors being taxed out of their homes

priorities.text: Says his campaign takes no PAC, party or dark money.
priorities.quote: My campaign takes no PAC money, no party money, no dark money.

statements.context: On his campaign site, under "Environmental Stewardship & Economic Growth"

statements.quote: Protect our borders; favor dialogue over war.
statements.context: On his campaign site, under "National Security & Smart Diplomacy"

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site says he has no personal platform and that his votes would follow constituent input collected through his Congress App, so no stances on specific guide issues are recorded. He is a write-in candidate. Statements are from his campaign site; priorities are from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
